previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A female patient with end-stage renal disease, systemic lupus erythematosus, and antiphospholipid syndrome was admitted for abdominal pain following an unsuccessful ERCP for choledocholithiasis. She developed post-ERCP pancreatitis with lipase over 20,000 and ileus, managed with bowel rest, IV fluids, pain control, and continued hemodialysis. Fevers early in admission were attributed to inflammation rather than infection, and antibiotics were discontinued. Her condition improved with normalization of lipase and liver enzymes, resolution of ileus, and advancement to a regular diet. Warfarin was restarted for anticoagulation, and lidocaine patches were added for chronic back pain. Psychiatry evaluated her for anxiety and delirium with visual hallucinations, which resolved with supportive care. She was discharged home with plans to reschedule ERCP outpatient, continue INR monitoring, and follow up with her primary care and mental health providers.
